drhp.business: The Company manufactures forged and machined components using cold forging, warm forging and hot forging, and has made a foray into castings. It has end-to-end capabilities from forging to machining including heat treatment, and supplies OEMs and Tier-1 suppliers in India and abroad, deriving the major share of its revenues from the Commercial Vehicle segment. Operations are in Jharkhand, Haryana and Pune, with a stated presence across Europe, North America and Asia.

risks.note: Stated verbatim as a SWOT weakness: "A large portion of revenue comes from the cyclical commercial vehicle segment making it vulnerable to market fluctuations in this sector." The Directors' Report reinforces it: "The Company derives the major share of its revenues from the Commercial Vehicle segment." This is the structural concentration risk of the business.
risks.risk: High dependency on the automotive sector, specifically the cyclical commercial vehicle segment

risks.note: Stated as a SWOT weakness: "Larger dependency on a geographical segment makes it vulnerable for any change in demand." The financial consequence was visible this year - export sales fell 19.94% year on year (figure not reproduced; disclosed in the Directors' Report financial-performance bullets) while the US Class 8 market was in a down cycle.
risks.risk: Geographical dependency / concentration on a single geographic segment

risks.note: The MD&A states that higher tariffs in the U.S. truck market increased input costs for OEMs and suppliers, particularly for steel, aluminium and imported components, pressuring margins, in some cases forcing price increases, and delaying order cycles. US Class 8 retail sales fell approximately 13-14% year on year to around 2,08,000-2,10,000 units, described as a "bottoming" phase. The European commercial vehicle market also contracted (EU van registrations -8.8%, trucks -6.2%, Western Europe HCV -4.2%).
risks.risk: US / export market cyclicality and tariff-driven cost inflation

risks.note: Stated as a SWOT threat: "Policy Change: Sudden changes in policies can affect demand including export demand." Concrete live instances in the text: the 2027 EPA low-NOx rules driving a US pre-buy then a potential air-pocket, and the US-China truce on tariffs and export controls that runs only until November 2026.
risks.risk: Sudden policy change, including changes affecting export demand

risks.note: Stated as a SWOT threat: "This can increase the cost of production or cost of sales of the Company." The MD&A adds that ongoing conflicts and escalation in the Middle East present emerging risks through global commodity price volatility, supply chain disruption and trade route uncertainty.
risks.risk: Geopolitical challenges raising cost of production / cost of sales

risks.note: Stated as a SWOT threat: "Technological advancements of both domestic and international competitors and price pressures." The MD&A notes continued industry consolidation and technology upgrades (precision machining, ring rolling) as the competitive baseline, with a shift towards value-added, precision-forged and machined components.

A joint fact-finding study by Independent External Agencies into discrepancies between book and physical inventory of work-in-progress, raw material and scrap was submitted on 14 June 2025. It confirmed the discrepancies arose from erroneous accounting entries and non-recording of rejections AT THE MANUFACTURING PLANTS, and quantified a resultant overstatement of inventory as at 31 March 2025 and 31 March 2024 (amounts deliberately not reproduced - they are financial-statement figures). The amounts were fully given effect to in the FY2024-25 statements, including restatement of the FY2023-24 comparatives. This is a durable governance/process risk at the plant level, not a one-off accounting entry.
